title: Quick Update
contentHtml:
Since being released from the ER I’ve done very little other than doctor visits and sit in my local McDonald’s, reading and scrolling online — a product of continuing lethargy and some lingering pain, and bad weather. While I’m feeling better, it’s been slow going, and the hope that I would soon be traveling again now seems a naive fantasy, certainly not overseas.

As one of my doctors said, the complications from getting ill in a foreign country are reason enough to stay in the US, particularly communication. While I’m sure the majority of employees in Asian hospitals speak passable to excellent English, lying in the ER is probably not the best place to test if someone really knows the subtleties of a language.

I have several doctor visits the next two weeks, so I’ll wait for more information, but it looks highly unlikely that I can go overseas the rest of this year1. Hopefully I can do shorter trips in a month or so — I’ve long wanted to spend considerably more time in California, specifically the San Francisco Bay area, Salinas Valley, and further north, up into Oregon and Washington. That’s the part of the US I know the least, so that’s probably where I will go when/if I get the green light2.

I’m sure everyone will be thinking, “Take it easy, enjoy your time at home, don’t stress,” and that’s very kind, and true, but when I’m tethered, limited where I can go and how much I can walk, I find myself invariably spending more time online, and that’s depressing. As much as I value insights from books, I prefer being out in the world, and the resulting essays which focus my thoughts on issues beyond the current thing. I don’t want this to become another “fight over the issue of the day” newsletter.

Regardless, I’m going to have to wait a little longer for my next essay, so my apologies. Thanks for the patience!

PS: Books I’ve recently read, are reading, and hope to write about in an upcoming post. I’m still looking for a good candidate to do a group read like we did with Moby Dick. I just started East of Eden, hoping it might fit!

1

In addition to the Pulmonary Embolism during the ER visit the doctor noticed an additional issue that needs following up. Hopefully nothing serious, but it will require a CAT scan, several tests by specialists, and here in the US that means up to two weeks just to get an appointment.

2

California is so physically gifted, with an embarrassment of riches, so there is more than a years worth of travel I would like to do in the state, but the walk from Richmond south to San Jose is what I want to do first.

Why focus on the east side rather than a walk from San Francisco to San Jose via Palo Alto? I think there is more going on that interest me on that side -- from the Kaiser shipyard that brought influx of workers during WW2, to the de-industrialization of 60s/70s that produced modern Oakland, to the post war high-tech boom (admittedly centered across the bay on the West side) that created a wealth/suburban Fremont, to recent immigration (drawn by high tech work), all overlay-ed on a ranching/Spanish past, its more on the east, or at least in an in your face way, than on the west. As well as the Spanish Missions, specifically Mission San José in Fremont.

Not to say the west side walk wouldn't be worth of a walk as well-- more focused on the military high-tech history, the Stanford academic to industry pipeline, the semi-conductor integrated circuit boom of the 60s, then of course our more current laptop/social-media industry, but if I have to choose one, I will go with the eastern walk

I would also like to, inspired by Steinbeck, travel down the Salinas Valley via bus. A Salinas, Soledad, King City, Paso Robles, San Luis Obispo sort of trip.

But that’s for another post!
